data.content_ref: inline:The target falsely dichotomizes 'logical derivation' and 'rational preference,' ignoring Popper's specific argument that preferring the better-corroborated theory is rational because it offers greater empirical content and testability (severity), not because it is more probable. By reducing the defense to mere 'convention' or 'psychology,' the target misses Popper's core distinction: one can rationally choose the theory that has withstood the severest tests as the best candidate for truth without claiming inductive proof of its probability, thus preserving a rational solution that is non-inductive.
